hook_text: A school built for 800 learners now has 1 400. A clinic queue starts before sunrise. What happens when a city grows faster than it can build?
clip_script: People arrive in the city faster than houses can be built. So shacks go up wherever there is empty land: river banks, steep slopes, beside the railway. One tap for dozens of families. Shared toilets, or none. Candles and paraffin for light, and fires that jump from shack to shack. In 2022, floods in KwaZulu-Natal killed more than four hundred people. Clinics overflow. Tuberculosis spreads in crowded rooms. Classrooms hold fifty learners. Children study by candlelight after queuing for water. What helps? Upgrading settlements where they are, mobile clinics, new classrooms, school meals. Cities bring opportunity. The challenge is to share it.
visual_style: A whiteboard settlement on a river bank with a single tap and a queue, then a classroom filling with figures and a clinic queue, ending with icons for upgrading, clinics and schools.
pacing: Building pressure, then a hopeful turn to solutions.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to evaluate how cities respond.
